Case Status — All Cases

One line per client: where the case stands, what is done, what is still needed, and what is holding it up. Nothing to enter — the AI Assistant reviews every case for you. Adding a note is optional.
⚠ About the red Case Progress Flag
Every case moves through 10 Case Progress stages in order, and each stage has its own sub-steps, each tracked as Not Started, In Progress, Completed or Not Applicable. A case is flagged in red when its current stage still has sub-steps open — the flag shows which stage the case is held at, who it is assigned to, each open sub-step with its status and outstanding items, and the overall progress across all 10 stages. A stage only becomes Completed when every sub-step is Completed or marked Not Applicable with a recorded reason. The case cannot move to the next stage until then, unless the stage is bypassed or marked Not Applicable as a whole with the Case Progress bypass passcode (set in Settings). Those stages are shown in amber with the reason. A green box means all 10 stages are complete. Click Open Stage … sub-steps on any flag to go straight to that stage in the Case Progress tab.

AI Lock & Security

Protects your Anthropic API key and every AI feature (AI Assistant, AI case review, letter and note drafting, estimate reading). While locked, your key is encrypted in this browser and nobody can use the AI without your passcode.
Easy passcodes (1234, 0000, 1111…) are refused. Your passcode is never saved anywhere — if you forget it, you reset it with a code emailed to you.
Lock settings, the API key and the security log are hidden until you unlock.
Anyone using this browser will be able to use your API key again.

One email for everything: alerts, wrong-passcode attempts, remote LOCK & UNLOCK buttons

Open the link from your phone or any computer and the AI locks within about 15 seconds on any screen where CaseWork is open. You unlock it again with your passcode. The link can only lock — it can never unlock. Keep it private.
Works only after you locked it from the email link. The unlock link is sent in a new email, works once, and expires in 8 hours. After “Lock AI now”, an idle auto-lock, or a page reload, only your passcode can unlock. Needs email delivery set up below.
Paste this ONE template into EmailJS (one-time): gives the red LOCK and green UNLOCK buttons
  1. In EmailJS open Email Templates → your template → Edit Content. If a menu appears, choose Code Editor.
  2. Press Ctrl+A (Mac: Cmd+A), Delete, and paste the code below, then Apply Changes and Save.
  3. Here, change “In the email, show it as” to red button and press “Email me the lock link”.
Alerts, wrong-passcode attempts, unlock/reset notices and test emails all use this one template. They show the red LOCK button; unlock requests show the green UNLOCK button instead. Use the checkboxes above to choose which events email you.

Email delivery (reset codes & alerts)

How to set up email (free, about 5 minutes)
  1. Make a free account at emailjs.com and under Email Services connect your Gmail (or other email). Copy the Service ID.
  2. Under Email Templates create a template. Set To Email to {{to_email}}, Subject to {{subject}}, and the body to {{message}}. Copy the Template ID.
  3. Under Account copy your Public Key. Paste all three above and press “Send me a test email”.
Without email set up, wrong attempts and unlocks are still recorded in the log below, but reset can only be done by erasing the saved API key.

Application Terms, Conditions & Program Rules

Printed on every Disaster Assistance Application (about 3,900 words, in two columns, between Supporting Documents and the signature block). The default is a template built on the Red Cross Fundamental Principles and the National VOAD Points of Consensus — have your leadership or legal counsel review it before relying on it, and edit it freely below. Use ## at the start of a line for an article heading; every other line prints as a clause.

Electronic Signature

Optional. When turned on, each client's case gets an Electronic Signature box (in Consent & Authorization and in Review & Submit) with a Sign on Client Screen button. It opens the application on a separate screen — a second monitor, a tablet, or a laptop facing the client — where the client reviews it, agrees to sign electronically, ticks each consent, and signs with a finger, stylus or mouse. Your own screen stays with you. The signature, date and time, and a fingerprint of the exact application signed are saved to the case and print on the application. The wording below is a template: have your leadership or legal counsel review it before relying on it. You can use {organization}, {jurisdiction}, {client} and {caseId} in any of it.
Electronic Signature Options
Windows computers only (Topaz’s software does not run on Chromebooks or Macs). Install Topaz’s free SigWeb on the Windows computer — topazsystems.com/sdks/sigweb.html › Download SigWeb Installer — plug the pad in by USB, and when Chrome asks to let this page reach devices on your local network, click Allow. Used for the client’s signature on the Client Screen of this computer and for your witness signature. If the pad is not found, signing falls back to the on-screen box. Phones and tablets that sign over Client’s Point or a link always sign on their own screen.
One-time EmailJS step: open your template → Attachments → Add Attachment → Variable Attachment. Parameter name signed_pdf, filename Signed-Application.pdf, content type PDF. EmailJS’s free plan limits each email to 50 KB, which is too small for the full application, so the PDF only arrives on a paid EmailJS plan. If an email fails, CaseWork tells you and you can download the PDF instead.

Client Tablet & Client’s Own Phone (over Wi-Fi)

Besides a second monitor, the client can sign on an Android tablet you keep as your client screen (pair it once) or on the client’s own phone (they scan a code). The application goes straight from this computer to that device over an encrypted direct connection — it is not stored on any server, and nothing is kept on the device after signing. The device opens the Client Signing Page: a small page with no client information in it. Put it online once (for example on your GitHub Pages, next to your other tools) and enter its address below. If CaseWork itself is opened from a web address (https://…), that address works as the signing page and you can leave this blank.

Case Progress Bypass Passcode

Case Progress is a restricted protocol: each of the 10 stages has its own sub-steps, and a case cannot move to the next stage until every sub-step is Completed or marked Not Applicable with a recorded reason. This passcode is the only way to bypass a stage that is not complete, or to mark a whole stage Not Applicable. Every bypass is recorded in the stage’s audit history and in that case’s Case Manager Comments with the reason and the sub-steps that were still open. The passcode is never stored — only a scrambled check of it.

Cloud Sync (via Dropbox / Google Drive / OneDrive)

This tool has no server, so it can't sync automatically over the internet on its own. What it can do is read and write one file that lives inside a folder your cloud storage app (Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, etc.) already syncs between your devices — the cloud app moves the bytes; this just knows how to read and write that one file. Set it up once per device, then click "Save to Sync File" before switching machines and "Load from Sync File" after you switch.
Works in Chrome, Edge, and other Chromium browsers. Not supported in Firefox or Safari — on those, use "Export All Cases" / "Import Case(s)" in the bottom bar instead, saving or opening the file from inside your cloud-synced folder; the effect is the same. Either way this is manual sync, triggered by you, not automatic or real-time — if you edit the same case on two devices before syncing, whichever save happens last will overwrite the other, so it's safest to treat one device as primary at a time.
